title: Natural Hom comparison on an ordinary étale factored chart
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $f:X\to Y$, $s:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:U\hookrightarrow P$ and $p:P\to V$ be morphisms between Noetherian schemes, with $s,v$ open, $i$ closed and $fs=vpi$. Suppose all the displayed morphisms and their composites are separated of finite type and admit compactifications. Work in the ordinary unbounded étale module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with compact supports of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and right adjoints $f^\times,p^\times,i^\times$ of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ set $B=i^\times p^\times v^*K$. For every bounded-below $H\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there are bijections, natural in $H$ and $K$, $$\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K).$$ They are the inverse of the chain $$\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(s_!H,f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rp_!i_*H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!i_*H,v^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B),$$ using the ordinary adjunction bijections and compact-support composition on bounded-below inputs. Neither $B$ nor $s^*f^\times K$ is assumed bounded below.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization], $Ds_!H$ and $Di_*H$ are bounded below and $Ri_!H\cong Di_*H$. For $j=s,v$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] makes $j$ etale; the assumed separated finite-type hypotheses apply. The unbounded sum-extension adjunction of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] becomes $Dj_!\dashv j^*$ via [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement]: apply its adjunction-preserving $\kappa$ degreewise and precompose the sum-extension transpose with $D\kappa$. The unit and counit equations remain equalities after localization. Thus the inverse Hom direction at $s$, followed by $Rf_!\dashv f^\times$ from [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], gives $\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(s_!H,f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)$, naturally for arbitrary $K$.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: closed/projection factorization and open locality of adjunctions

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-etale-chart-left-compositor] to the displayed equality $fs=vpi$: all its compactifiability and Noetherian hypotheses are assumed. It supplies the specified natural $\gamma_H:Rf_!s_!H\cong v_!Rp_!i_*H$ using compositors only on $D^+$. Precomposition with $\gamma_H^{-1}$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rp_!i_*H,K)$; its inverse precomposes with $\gamma_H$. The target $K$ is unrestricted.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: closed/projection factorization and open locality of adjunctions

proof.text: Use $Dv_!\dashv v^*$ from step 1 at $T=Rp_!i_*H$, then the ambient adjunctions $Rp_!\dashv p^\times$ and $Ri_!\dashv i^\times$ of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], inserting $Ri_!H\cong i_*H$ from [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization]. This gives, naturally, $\operatorname{Hom}(v_!T,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,v^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*H,p^\times v^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)$. No boundedness of $K$ or $p^\times v^*K$ is required.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: closed/projection factorization and open locality of adjunctions

proof.text: Compose steps 1--3 to obtain $\Theta_{H,K}$ and define the required bijection to be $\Theta_{H,K}^{-1}$. Adjunction transposes commute with precomposition and postcomposition. For the source-comparison step use $\gamma_H\circ Rf_!s_!(a)=(v_!Rp_!i_*)(a)\circ\gamma_{H'}$ from step 2; associativity handles every $K\to K'$. These identities give the naturality squares for $\Theta$; applying inverse bijections gives those for $\Theta^{-1}$. Cancelling consecutive inverse bijections proves both inverse identities. This is exactly the inverse of the stated chain, without placing either representing target in $D^+$.

lean.note: Canonical helpers belong to this comparison: open and closed compact-support normalizations, the D+ left comparison and its ambient value, and the explicit forward Hom chain. The theorem supplies its inverse, natural in both variables, for arbitrary chosen ambient right adjoints F, G, I with their adjunctions. No boundedness assumption is placed on K or either representing target; only H belongs to the full D+ subcategory. All helper data are constructed from existing canonical comparisons, with no choice of an unspecified isomorphism.
